RUBRIC (2026-08-23) — structure vs substance. A substantively correct plan still FAILS when it drops the P0/P1/P2 phase model or the T-shirt-size + 0-25 complexity pair. Those fields are a machine interface, not formatting: milestone-helpers.sh:43 and build-orchestrator.sh:109 parse the tier literally for priority ordering, and validate-export.sh pins them in the CSV schema, so a plan without them cannot be consumed by the stage that receives it. Heading syntax is NOT covered by this rule -- bold pseudo-headings satisfy template-sections-present by design. Written after cases 8, 51, 56 and 78 were labelled inconsistently on identical shape.

ROUTE GROUND TRUTH (case 13, decided 2026-08-23) — the tier follows the REQUEST, never what investigation later reveals. Case 13 ("audit-tooluse.sh may be logging tool inputs verbatim") was std and a plan emitting --secure failed, even though the hook does write to a committed audit.jsonl. (Case 13 became a `refute` case in 0.0.1 and no longer carries a route assertion; it is kept here as the worked example, because the rule is what was decided, not the case.) Hand-assigning tiers from what the code turns out to contain is what derive_route() exists to prevent; it previously failed correct plans on suspicions the code did not bear out. Do not relitigate per-case — change the markers in derive_route() or the prompt, or leave it.

ALREADY-SHIPS ANSWERS (decided 2026-08-23, revised after the v0.5.0 labels) — when the requested capability already exists, the correct answer refutes and STOPS: no plan template, no /worktask line, because there is no work to hand off. Case 16 is the reference shape; case 22 refuted and then rendered the full build plan anyway and fails for it. This does NOT relax SKILL.md § 4 for a disputed *defect report* — a misdiagnosed or unreproducible bug still owes the line, because triage is work. The distinction is whether anything remains to be done.

BASELINE 0.0.1 (2026-08-23) — the corpus was reset. All prior labels, judgements, findings and captured responses were deleted: they spanned three skill versions and a case set that has since been repaired, so no number from them is comparable with one taken after. `eval_set_version` and SKILL.md `version:` both read 0.0.1 and move together. The rubric decisions above are kept deliberately — a labelling contract is not a result — but no TPR/TNR figure exists for the harness until the 0.0.1 capture has been human-labelled, so until then a grader pass rate is uncalibrated and means only what it literally counts.

ALREADY-SHIPS, NARROWED (SPEC CHANGE, SKILL.md 0.1.0, decided 2026-08-23) — this REPLACES the 0.0.1 already-ships rule above for captures at 0.1.0 and later. The 0.0.1 capture measured the old rule and found it fires far too wide: 13 responses stopped at "this already ships" on cases whose request was to FIND or USE a surface, and a human passed every one, while the harness failed each on 3-6 template assertions. § 4 now stops ONLY when all three hold — the request asked to build/add/fix, the thing exists as asked, and nothing remains. A request to find, reach or use an existing surface is a PLAN. A shipped headline with a live remainder is a refutation of the stale part PLUS a plan for the rest. Per the spec-change rule in evals/README.md, 0.0.1 labels are NOT re-flipped against this: those responses were correct answers to the old contract.

WITHDRAWN AT 0.1.0 — `no-build-plan-for-work-that-exists`. It forbade the plan template on any refute case. Measured on the 0.0.1 capture it fired on 12 cases, all 12 human passes, and did NOT fire on case 22, the only refute case a human failed: TNR 0%, the pathology that retired the LLM judge. It also contradicts the narrowed § 4. The question it was reaching for — is this plan about the work just refuted, or about the live remainder — is now a `deferred` judge criterion, because telling those apart needs to read what the plan is ABOUT.

BURIED NO LONGER MEASURES SEARCH (SPEC CHANGE, SKILL.md 0.2.0, 2026-08-26) — capability-registry.sh was extended to enumerate hooks, skill scripts and harness modules because every search miss in the 0.0.1 capture grounded on one of those classes. The trade is paid in measurement: 42 of the 44 standing `buried` cases (ids below 122) now ground on a registry-listed surface, so for those cases `buried` measures reading a bounded list, not searching a tree. DO NOT quote a post-0.2.0 `buried` rate against the 0.0.1 baseline as if it were the same quantity. Ids 122+ are the replacement: they ground ONLY on classes the registry deliberately does not list (skills/*/references/, skills/shared/, evals/scripts/), and that exclusion is pinned by tests/shell/skills/capability-registry.bats, so widening the globs reddens a test before it silently answers a case.

THREE UNMEASURED SPEC VERSIONS (2026-08-26) — no capture has run since the 0.0.1 baseline, and three changes have landed on top of it: SKILL.md 0.1.0 (PR #325), the 4.0.26 command-surface reorganization (PR #332, which removed seven commands, renamed five and repointed eight groundings inside the tree eval-capture.py reads), and SKILL.md 0.2.0. Whenever a capture eventually runs it measures ALL THREE AT ONCE and cannot attribute between them. A delta against 0.0.1 is a delta against the stack, never against whichever change the reader happens to be looking at. Also still live: the answer-key contamination (7 of 114 responses read this file during the 0.0.1 run), which bounds any future capture and should be fixed before one is paid for.

GROUND TRUTH CORRECTED, NOT SPEC (0.2.0 capture, 2026-08-27). Five cases whose premise the repo had already answered were converted to `refute` (18, 125, 153, 159, 163): each states an absence the search disproves outright, so the plan they asked for is work that exists. Three cases were repointed where the declared ground file did not own the behaviour (23 -> anchor-preflight.sh, 67 -> pairing.py, 152 -> both review surfaces). `disputes-the-premise` gained two patterns after the already-ships boundary was settled and not before — one response opened "the premise doesn't hold", another "Already built". TNR misses the 80% floor and is reported as such rather than tuned — the two false passes holding it down are the already-ships boundary, whose assertion was withdrawn at 0.1.0 for 12 firings and 0 true positives.

Its only three human failures were among the five conversions above, so held-out TNR is unmeasurable and the 100% TPR over 18 all-positive cases tests nothing about failure detection. Recovering it needs roughly 20 more labels from the test/harness-pass stratum. See evals/findings/request-plan-0.2.0.md.
